title: Battery Storage Maintenance Log Form
subtitle: An original battery storage workflow that carries planned or condition-based maintenance through safe release, with explicit qualified-review, stop-work, escalation, and accountable handoff controls.
description: A workflow-complete battery storage maintenance log form for the stationary battery energy storage system that captures exact identity, domain observations, supporting evidence, decisions, exceptions, responsible owners, and closeout without replacing professional judgment or the organization's controlling procedures.
use_case: Use when service personnel need one record for maintenance trigger, asset baseline, work-control references, recurring events, readings, deferred defects, and qualified return-to-service approval. The energy storage operations lead owns routing, and closure requires documented evidence, disposition of restrictions, and acceptance by the designated reviewer.

sections.title: Battery storage maintenance log identity and ownership
sections.guidance: Define the maintained system, service interval, operating owner, and review period.

sections.title: Battery storage asset baseline and maintenance readiness
sections.guidance: Reconcile the exact asset and known condition before maintenance or testing begins.

blocks.label: Planned maintenance task set
items: Confirm system, chemistry, rack, module, PCS, inverter, and BMS identities
Coordinate dispatch state, critical loads, outage limits, and manufacturer support
Establish site-specific electrical, stored-energy, thermal, and access controls
Review alarms, events, trends, SOC, SOH, temperatures, and isolation status remotely
Inspect enclosure, HVAC, detection, suppression, seals, labels, and clearances
Complete only manufacturer-approved cleaning, filter, connection, or component work
Record module or string values using an approved method and qualified person
Perform authorized communications, control, protection, and functional checks
Reconcile alarms, settings, firmware, parts, photos, and service evidence
Maintain restriction or return the system through explicit qualified release

sections.title: Battery storage work control and safe service boundary
sections.guidance: Record the qualified roles and controlling references; do not use this log as the controlling procedure.

blocks.label: Service readiness confirmations
items: Current procedure, manufacturer information, and applicable requirements were reviewed
Asset boundaries, every energy source, and affected systems were identified
Authorized, affected, contractor, and operations roles were coordinated
Isolation, stored-energy control, and verification references are complete
Required tools, instruments, parts, and protective controls are available
Test, temporary energization, and return-to-service steps have explicit authority
Customer, public, traffic, environmental, and critical-service impacts are controlled
Stop conditions and emergency escalation path are understood

blocks.label: Maintenance stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: Do not open, enter, touch, reset, or approach a battery system showing heat, smoke, flame, hissing, odor, swelling, leaking, water intrusion, impact damage, or an isolation alarm. Keep people clear and activate the site emergency plan. Stored or stranded energy may remain after shutdown; only designated qualified personnel may assess isolation, recovery, and return to service. Maintenance stays restricted when isolation, stored energy, system condition, or work scope is unknown. Only the designated authorized person may direct changes to controls and the qualified release owner may approve return to service.

sections.title: Battery storage maintenance events, condition, and readings
sections.guidance: Create a traceable history of work completed, condition found, evidence, and deferred action.

fields.label: Wear pattern, recurring fault, consumable trend, configuration change, and supporting evidence

sections.title: Battery storage exceptions, stop conditions, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make every unresolved condition visible with an immediate control, owner, due point, and final disposition.

blocks.label: Stop-condition screen
items: Smoke, flame, rapid heat rise, hissing, popping, or unusual odor
Swelling, deformation, electrolyte residue, leak, or damaged cell enclosure
Thermal, gas, fire-detection, suppression, or ventilation alarm
Water intrusion, flooding, condensation, or damaged environmental seal
Impact, penetration, dropped module, damaged cable, or exposed conductor
Unknown isolation, stranded charge, backfeed, or reaccumulating stored energy
Manufacturer stop condition or emergency-plan activation threshold
Any entry or task beyond the person's training, PPE, tools, or authorization
blocks.guidance: Check any condition observed or reported; checking an item does not mean the condition is controlled.

blocks.label: Qualified-person and stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: Do not open, enter, touch, reset, or approach a battery system showing heat, smoke, flame, hissing, odor, swelling, leaking, water intrusion, impact damage, or an isolation alarm. Keep people clear and activate the site emergency plan. Stored or stranded energy may remain after shutdown; only designated qualified personnel may assess isolation, recovery, and return to service.

blocks.label: Exception and escalation register
blocks.guidance: Link each maintenance exception to supporting evidence and keep it open until disposition is recorded.

sections.title: Battery storage decision, handoff, and accountable closeout
sections.guidance: Record the decision, remaining limitations, next action, and the people accountable for acceptance.

blocks.label: Closeout completeness
items: Stationary battery energy storage system identity and location were reconciled
Observed facts, measurements, and evidence references are complete
Decision authority and applicable review requirements were confirmed
Stop conditions, restrictions, and open exceptions remain visible
Customer, operations, or site handoff was recorded
Next action, owner, due point, and record-retention route are explicit

fields.label: Limitations, assumptions, restrictions, customer message, and next-action context

blocks.label: Accountable review and handoff
blocks.guidance: Signatures acknowledge the recorded decision and handoff; they do not waive unresolved restrictions.
